note: Adjudicated accidental variants (orthography and punctuation). Substantive text agrees across both witnesses with zero variants.

adjudicated.ruling: Comma after the object, with DO. This is not the apposition case the corpus has repeatedly left unbroken: what follows is a participial clause with its own object (tuam deprecántes cleméntiam), and the comma marks a real syntactic seam.

The j-form against this edition's i-form, by the house rule in ORTHOGRAPHY.md. This edition prints i because the books it edits do: the 1962 typical edition sets Iesu, Ioánnem, iube and maiestátis throughout, and so does the Mszał Rzymski of the Tyniec Benedictines (Pallottinum, Poznań 1963), which is the book a Polish reader is most likely to hold. The mid-century hand missals print j; neither spelling is a different word, and the apparatus records theirs.

No comma before the 'et' joining the second modifier of salúte, with DO and with the corpus rulings at ordinarium.confiteor w028 and ordinarium.iudica-me w038: nostra and totíus mundi both depend on salúte and are not separated from each other.

Comma closing the phrase, with DO. It answers the comma after tuæ, which both witnesses print: the two fence 'pro nostra et totíus mundi salúte' as one interposed phrase between the place (in conspéctu) and the verb (ascéndat).
